title: Enfortumab vedotin · monotherapy
context_label: Advanced urothelial cancer · after platinum and immunotherapy
indication_text: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer after both platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor.
purpose: Help control advanced urothelial cancer previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor.
schedule_summary: Enfortumab vedotin is given on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. The starting dose is 1.25 mg/kg, capped at 125 mg per dose. The team may hold, reduce or stop treatment for side effects. Treatment continues while appropriate according to benefit and tolerance.
administration_text: The infusion runs over 30 minutes through a carefully checked intravenous line. Tests, review and observation add to the visit time. Tell the nurse immediately if there is pain or swelling around the line.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose on days 1, 8 and 15 in cycle 1, then on day 1 of later cycles in the NCCP schedule, with additional tests as clinically needed. Lipase and HbA1c on day 1 if indicated. Review skin and nerve symptoms throughout; assess eye or breathing symptoms promptly.
safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital instructions. This information supports a discussion; it does not authorise treatment.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999.

agents.name: Enfortumab vedotin
agents.mechanism: Delivers a cell-division inhibitor to cells bearing nectin-4
agents.explanation: An antibody attaches to a protein called nectin-4 and delivers a chemotherapy payload that disrupts cell division. Healthy skin, nerves and other tissues can also be affected. This is not a checkpoint immunotherapy medicine.
agents.watch: Report any rash early, especially blistering, fever or mouth/eye/genital sores; also report thirst, frequent urination, numbness or new breathing symptoms.
risks: Skin rash, sometimes severe or life-threatening including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis; serious reactions may occur in the first cycle
High blood glucose and diabetic ketoacidosis, including in people without known diabetes
Numbness, tingling or weakness from peripheral neuropathy, sometimes lasting
Dry eyes, blurred vision and corneal problems
Lung inflammation, sometimes severe or fatal
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Fatigue, reduced appetite, taste changes, nausea, diarrhoea and hair loss
Infusion reactions and tissue injury from leakage outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm

anatomy: New cough, fever or breathlessness needs urgent assessment.
Report blurred vision, eye pain, dry eyes or mouth sores.
Thirst, frequent urine, vomiting, confusion or deep breathing needs urgent help.
Report persistent diarrhoea, poor intake or difficulty drinking.
Report reduced urine or inability to keep fluids down.
Fever, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Report any rash early; blistering, peeling or fever with rash needs urgent help.
Report numbness, tingling, weakness or balance problems before the next dose.

evidence.title: EV-301 · 2021 primary report
evidence.summary: EV-301 randomised 608 people previously treated with platinum and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor. Median overall survival was 12.88 months with enfortumab versus 8.97 months with investigator-selected chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% confidence interval 0.56–0.89).
evidence.intro: EV-301 randomised 608 people previously treated with platinum and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor. Median overall survival was 12.88 months with enfortumab versus 8.97 months with investigator-selected chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% confidence interval 0.56–0.89).
evidence.caveat: These group medians do not predict an individual lifespan. The result concerns later-line monotherapy and must not be substituted for evidence about first-line enfortumab/pembrolizumab.
evidence.interpretation: These group medians do not predict an individual lifespan. The result concerns later-line monotherapy and must not be substituted for evidence about first-line enfortumab/pembrolizumab.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Help control advanced urothelial cancer previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor. This page covers enfortumab alone after prior platinum and checkpoint immunotherapy. It is distinct from first-line enfortumab plus pembrolizumab, which has a different schedule and risk context.

Enfortumab vedotin is given on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. The starting dose is 1.25 mg/kg, capped at 125 mg per dose. The team may hold, reduce or stop treatment for side effects. Treatment continues while appropriate according to benefit and tolerance.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
